readme: One telephone call, as a switchboard sends it: the messages a jambonz WebSocket application receives, from the call arriving to the caller putting the handset down. Nothing here is a recording of a real call and nothing in it identifies anybody — the identifiers are invented, and the two numbers are from the range reserved for fiction, which belongs to nobody. It is a fixture: the checks replay it through the adapter and expect a real booking in the diary at the end, which is how the translation is shown to be right without a telephone line.
shape: Message shapes and verb properties follow the published jambonz documentation for the WebSocket call-control API. Where a field's shape could not be checked against it, the field is left out rather than guessed at, and the README names what is missing: the SIP envelope on a new session, the vendor-specific block a recogniser attaches to a transcript, and everything to do with digits. The notes below sit outside the messages for the same reason — a message here is a message, with nothing added to it.

call.note: The call arrives. This must be answered within five seconds or it is dropped.
What the caller said, as the switchboard heard it. This is the whole of the audio anything here ever sees.

alternatives.transcript: I need an MRI of the left knee without contrast

call.note: The caller went to find their prescription and said nothing at all. Nothing is sent to the agent; the question is asked again, in the agent's own words.
The name to put it under.
Picking one of the times the agent read out. On a telephone they are sentences rather than a numbered list, which is why an answer like this one has to be understood by position.
Confirming it. The answer to this one is the booking, so what goes back is the reference said out loud and then the call ending.
The handset goes down. Nothing is sent back: a status notification is not acknowledged.
